answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks through time-locked collateral staking. Agents must escrow scarce tokens in a registry contract that broadcasts a periodic verification lantern. This forces an attacker to commit significant liquid capital per identity, bearing real opportunity costs across an extended operational horizon. Slashing penalties reach their punitive zenith if coordinated fraud is proven. However, high capital barriers disproportionately exclude low-budget agents.
